blocks.text: Setting up your Mac for medical billing data

Your Mac handles Excel well, but configuration matters. Ensure you are running a recent version of macOS to keep Microsoft 365 stable. If your Excel feels slow, check your RAM. Aim for 8 GB or more to handle large claim logs without lag.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for claims specialists

Stop clicking through ribbons. Use these shortcuts to save seconds on every entry. To edit a cell, press Fn + F2. To select a full column of claim IDs, press Control + Space. To insert the current date, which is vital for audit trails, press Control + Semicolon.

Excel often strips leading zeros from patient IDs or insurance codes. This ruins your data. Always format these columns as Text before pasting your data. Right-click the column header, select Format Cells, and choose Text. This preserves the integrity of your medical record numbers.

Use the COUNTIFS function to track denials by payer. If you have a column for Payer and a column for Status, use a formula like =COUNTIFS(A:A, "BlueCross", B:B, "Denied"). This gives you an instant view of where your work is stuck.
